description: Revised final candidate taxonomy for classifying MCP servers by dominant user-facing functionality. Version 2 restores source-control/software-collaboration as a recurring category after review found that GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket servers were being scattered across unrelated categories.

assignment_policy.primary_rule: Assign each MCP server to the category that best captures its dominant user-facing capability, not its installation method, framework, or generic MCP protocol implementation.
evidence_priority: repository name only when other evidence is sparse
noise_to_ignore: installation commands such as npm install, pip install, docker run, uv run
generic build/test/lint/deploy instructions unless they are the exposed server capability
authentication setup unless identity/security is the core function
tie_breakers: Prefer domain-specific categories over generic data access when the server performs domain actions such as trading, payments, vulnerability scanning, or infrastructure control.
Prefer Infrastructure and Operations over Local Execution and Automation when the server manages cloud/container/service lifecycle rather than merely executing local commands.
Prefer Local Execution and Automation when the exposed capability is shell/filesystem/browser control even if the README mentions data retrieval.
Prefer Source Control and Software Collaboration when the server exposes repository, commit, branch, pull/merge request, release, issue, or code-review operations.
Prefer Agent and AI Tooling only when prompts, memory, RAG, embeddings, model routing, or agent orchestration are first-class server functions rather than marketing context.
Use Other Specialized Integrations only when evidence is sparse or the integration belongs to a long-tail domain not represented by the major categories.
Use Other Specialized Integrations only when evidence is sparse or the integration belongs to a long-tail domain not represented by the recurring categories.

categories.name: Data and Knowledge Access
categories.description: Retrieval, querying, search, summarization, or exposure of structured data, documents, knowledge bases, web content, and public or SaaS records.
include_criteria: Search engines, web/content retrieval, news, RSS, social/public content lookup
Knowledge bases, documentation, wiki, papers, notes, and document retrieval
Database and data warehouse querying when the main purpose is information access
SaaS record retrieval where the server primarily reads or searches content
exclude_criteria: Financial, commerce, or blockchain data with trading/payment/wallet semantics
Infrastructure control-plane management of databases, cloud, or services
Substantial computation, visualization, or reporting over data
Browser automation where UI control is the primary capability
Repository, commit, branch, pull/merge request, release, or code-review operations

categories.name: Agent and AI Tooling
categories.description: Prompting, memory, RAG, embeddings, model routing, AI generation, and agent-oriented tooling for AI assistants.
include_criteria: Prompt libraries, prompt execution, or prompt templates exposed as server functionality
Agent memory, planning, orchestration, or agent-to-agent workflows
RAG, embeddings, vectorization, semantic search infrastructure for AI assistants
Model-provider routing or AI generation services when that is the primary function
exclude_criteria: Generic statements that an MCP server helps Claude or LLMs
Ordinary retrieval servers that do not expose AI/agent tooling as a primary function
Image/audio generation better classified as Analytics and Creative Tools when media production is dominant
GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket repository automation without agent, prompt, memory, RAG, or model-routing functionality

categories.name: Infrastructure and Operations
categories.description: Cloud resources, containers, deployments, observability, gateways, proxies, and service operations.
include_criteria: Cloud service administration and control-plane operations
Docker, Kubernetes, container, deployment, CI/CD, or service lifecycle management
Observability, logs, metrics, monitoring, tracing, and incident operations
Gateways, API proxies, MCP aggregators, routing, and service orchestration
exclude_criteria: Dockerfiles or deployment instructions included only for installing the server
Local shell/filesystem automation without service or infrastructure management
Source repository workflows such as commits and pull requests

categories.name: Productivity and Communication
categories.description: Tasks, calendars, messaging, email, meetings, tickets, project boards, and workflow coordination.
include_criteria: Task, todo, reminder, project board, ticket, and workflow management
Calendar, scheduling, meetings, availability, and event management
Email, messaging, team chat, and social communication integrations
Developer issue tracking when the dominant purpose is task/work coordination rather than repository operations
exclude_criteria: Git commits, branches, pull requests, or code review as dominant functionality
Public social-media search or content retrieval without communication/workflow actions
Infrastructure workflow orchestration

categories.name: Financial and Blockchain Services
categories.description: Financial data, trading, payments, ecommerce, crypto, wallets, smart contracts, and on-chain analysis.
include_criteria: Market data, trading, portfolio, banking, accounting, invoices, and payments
Ecommerce operations such as products, orders, customers, and storefront actions
Cryptocurrency, wallets, smart contracts, tokens, NFTs, and blockchain analytics
exclude_criteria: Generic company or economic data retrieval without financial operations
Blockchain development documentation retrieval without wallet/on-chain functionality
Security scanning of blockchain code when security is dominant
examples: Ethereum/Solana wallet and on-chain analysis servers

categories.name: Analytics and Creative Tools
categories.description: Computation, analytics, visualization, media generation, design, and peripheral utilities.
include_criteria: Math, statistics, computation, simulation, optimization, analysis, and visualization
Charts, dashboards, reports, notebooks, spreadsheets, CSV/Excel analysis
Image, video, audio, design, drawing, transcription, QR, camera, hardware, and peripheral utility tools
exclude_criteria: Simple data retrieval without computation or transformation
Financial or blockchain analytics with domain-specific wallet/trading semantics
Browser automation when UI control rather than media output is dominant
Source-control analytics or code-review workflows where repository collaboration is dominant

categories.name: Local Execution and Automation
categories.description: Local command execution, filesystem operations, browser automation, and workspace control.
include_criteria: Executing local shell, terminal, Python/Node snippets, or OS commands
Reading, writing, moving, or searching local files and directories
Browser, UI, webpage, screenshot, scraping, crawler, or web-app automation
Workspace and desktop automation
exclude_criteria: Cloud/container infrastructure management
Repository collaboration as a Git workflow
Public web search where browser control is not the core exposed capability

categories.name: Security and Access Control
categories.description: Vulnerability scanning, security auditing, identity, secrets, permissions, policy, and compliance.
include_criteria: Security scanning, vulnerability detection, penetration testing, threat intelligence, and CVE analysis
Access control, IAM, identity, permissions, secrets, vaults, policies, and compliance
Security-focused audit of systems, dependencies, browser extensions, repositories, or infrastructure
exclude_criteria: Authentication required merely to access another service
Generic OAuth setup for a productivity/data/infrastructure server
General infrastructure management without security/audit focus
General repository operations that are not security audit, secret scanning, policy, or vulnerability analysis

categories.name: Source Control and Software Collaboration
categories.description: Source-code repository operations, including Git hosting APIs, commits, branches, pull/merge requests, code review, releases, and repository-file workflows.
include_criteria: Exposed tools call GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea, Forgejo, Sourcegraph, or Azure DevOps repository APIs
The server creates, updates, lists, or reviews commits, branches, repository files, pull requests, merge requests, diffs, releases, or tags
Issue workflows are included only when they are part of repository collaboration rather than general task management
exclude_criteria: Generic mention of a GitHub repository as project hosting only
Jira/Linear/Trello issue workflows without repository operations
Infrastructure deployment from repositories when deployment or cloud operations are dominant
Security scans of repositories when vulnerability/security auditing is dominant
examples: repository file and branch management servers

categories.name: Other Specialized Integrations
categories.description: Long-tail domain-specific MCP servers that do not fall into the major recurring categories.
include_criteria: Weather, maps, travel, games, education, smart home, IoT, and other specialized domains when no major category dominates
Sparse or template-like repositories where evidence is insufficient for confident classification
Low-frequency integrations that are too small to justify a top-level category
exclude_criteria: Any server with clear evidence for one of the eight major categories
A server should not be assigned here solely because it is unusual if its dominant function matches another category
examples: Template/example servers with insufficient functional evidence
